questions.q: Correct statement(s) about the compounds $\textbf{X}$, $\textbf{Y}$ and $\textbf{Z}$ is(are)
options: $\textbf{X}$ is used for sterilizing drinking water.
$\textbf{Z}$ is used in the enrichment of $^{235}\text{U}$.
$\textbf{Y}$ is a stronger Lewis base than ammonia.
questions.solution:
From the given reactions, we can identify the compounds $\textbf{X}$, $\textbf{Y}$, and $\textbf{Z}$ as follows:

Reaction 1: $\text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{HCl (conc.)} \rightarrow \text{MnCl}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$
The greenish-yellow gas $\textbf{X}$ is $\text{Cl}_2$.

Reaction 2: $\text{NH}_3 + 3\text{Cl}_2 \text{ (excess)} \rightarrow \text{NCl}_3 + 3\text{HCl}$
Compound $\textbf{Y}$ is $\text{NCl}_3$.

Reaction 3: $\text{Cl}_2 + 3\text{F}_2 \text{ (excess)} \xrightarrow{573\text{ K}} 2\text{ClF}_3$
Compound $\textbf{Z}$ is $\text{ClF}_3$.

Evaluating the given statements:
(A) $\text{Cl}_2$ is widely used as a disinfectant for sterilizing drinking water. This statement is correct.

(B) In $\text{NCl}_3$, the nitrogen atom is $sp^3$ hybridized and possesses one lone pair of electrons. This gives it a trigonal pyramidal structure, not a planar one. This statement is incorrect.

(C) $\text{ClF}_3$ is used in the enrichment of $^{235}\text{U}$ because it reacts with uranium to produce the volatile compound $\text{UF}_6$ ($\text{U} + 3\text{ClF}_3 \rightarrow \text{UF}_6 + 3\text{ClF}$). This statement is correct.

(D) $\text{NCl}_3$ is a weaker Lewis base than $\text{NH}_3$. The highly electronegative chlorine atoms withdraw electron density from the nitrogen atom via the -I effect, making the lone pair less available for donation compared to ammonia. This statement is incorrect.

Answer: $\textbf{X}$ is used for sterilizing drinking water.; $\textbf{Z}$ is used in the enrichment of $^{235}\text{U}$.

options: $\textbf{P}$ has two lone pairs of electrons on the central atom.

$\text{Xe(g)} + 2\text{F}_2\text{(g)} \xrightarrow[\text{1 : 5 ratio}]{\text{873 K, 7 bar}} \text{XeF}_4$

questions.q: Dissolving $1 . 24g$ of white phosphorous in boiling $NaOH$ solution in an inert atmosphere gives a gas $Q$. The amount of ${CuSO}_{4}$ (in $g$) required to completely consume the gas $Q$ is____[Given: Atomic mass of $H = 1, O = 16, Na = 23, P = 31, S = 32, Cu = 63$]
questions.solution:
$\mathop{{P}_{4}}_{1 . 24g} + 3NaOH + 3{H}_{2}O \to {PH}_{3} + 3{NaH}_{2}{PO}_{2}$

Number of moles of ${P}_{4} = \dfrac{Givenmass}{molarmass} = \dfrac{1 . 24}{124} = 0 . 01moles$

As $NaOH$ is present in excess. So, amount of phosphine formed is $0 . 01$ mole (as ${P}_{4}$ is limiting reagent)

$\mathop{2{PH}_{3}}_{0 . 01mole} + 3{CuSO}_{4} \to {Cu}_{3}{P}_{2} + 3{H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$

Since 2 moles of phosphine required 3 moles of ${CuSO}_{4}$.

Amount of ${CuSO}_{4}$ required $= \dfrac{3 \times 0 . 01}{2}$ mole

Mass of ${CuSO}_{4}$ (in $g$) required $= \dfrac{0 . 03}{2} \times \left(63 + 32 + 16 \times 4\right)$

$= \dfrac{0 . 03}{2} \times 159$

$= 2 . 38g$

questions.q: $\text{ Aqueous solution of } \mathrm{Na}}_{2}  \mathrm{~S}$}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{3} \text{ on reaction with } \mathrm{Cl}$}_{2} $\text{ gives }$
questions.solution:
Sodium thiosulphate, $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{ S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ gets oxidised by chlorine water.

$\mathrm{Na}}_{2}  \mathrm{ S}$}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{3}+4  \mathrm{Cl}$}_{2}+5 $\mathrm{H}}_{2}  \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow2  \mathrm{NaHSO}$}_{4}+8 $\mathrm{HCl} \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{ S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ gets oxidised by $\mathrm{FeCl}_3$ into $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{ S}_4 \mathrm{O}_6$
2 $\mathrm{Na}}_{2}  \mathrm{ S}$}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{3}+2  \mathrm{FeCl}$}_{3} \longrightarrow $\mathrm{Na}}_{2}  \mathrm{ S}$}_{4} $\mathrm{O}}_{6}+2  \mathrm{FeCl}$}_{2}+2 $\mathrm{NaCl}$ Further, $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{ S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ decomposes on treatment with dilute acids

$\mathrm{Na}}_{2}  \mathrm{ S}$}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{3}+2  \mathrm{HCl} \longrightarrow2  \mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{SO}$}_{2}+$\mathrm{S}+\mathrm{H}}_{2} \mathrm{O}$
questions.explanation:
Sodium thiosulphate, $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ gets oxidised by chlorine water.
$$
\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3+4 \mathrm{Cl}_2+5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NaHSO}_4+8 \mathrm{HCl}
$$
$\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ gets oxidised by $\mathrm{FeCl}_3$ into $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_4 \mathrm{O}_6$
$$
2 \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3+2 \mathrm{FeCl}_3 \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_4 \mathrm{O}_6+2 \mathrm{FeCl}_2+2 \mathrm{NaCl}
$$
Further, $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ decomposes on treatment with dilute acids
$$
\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_2 \mathrm{O}_3+2 \mathrm{HCl} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{SO}_2+\mathrm{S}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}
$$
